method: Wash the vegetables. Chop onion and peppers where listed; slice tomato where listed and keep raw meat preparation separate.
Cut the 250g baby potatoes into roughly 1 cm cubes. Simmer in a saucepan of water for about 6–8 minutes, continuing until a knife enters the centre easily. Drain thoroughly and let steam escape.

Use half the measured olive oil in a frying pan. Dice the chicken into roughly 2 cm pieces. Cook the chicken breast thoroughly, turning regularly. Check the thickest piece is steaming hot through the centre. A clean probe should read 70°C for 2 minutes. The chicken must have no pink flesh and its juices should run clear. Transfer to a clean plate.

Heat the remaining half of the measured olive oil in the frying pan. Add the drained potatoes and turn occasionally until golden. Add the onion, mixed peppers; cook until softened, with spinach wilted and excess liquid evaporated where listed.
Return the fully cooked chicken breast to the pan and heat through.
Stir in the listed flavour ingredients (2g paprika, 1g chilli powder, 1g garlic powder, 1g dried oregano), mixing powders and liquids evenly; heat any beans or mushrooms until steaming hot.
Check the potatoes are tender inside, the vegetables are cooked and the whole hash is hot. Serve the full measured portion immediately.

review.notes: Golden small potato cubes, browned chicken breast pieces, softened onion and mixed peppers; no sausage despite legacy recipe id; no spinach or garnish.
